column1: # PO ruling P14 (2026-10-31), "Only what the papers say": চ্যাট tells what is written about a medicine (its name, strength,
# how to take it) and never what it is for, what it treats or what kind of medicine it is; that goes to the doctor or the
# pharmacist. Written before the guard, both directions on both sides.

column3: text      (tab-separated; a line starting with # is a comment)

column1: # answer rows are model text, checked through AnswerCheck exactly as the pipeline checks it, with
#   {{rx:2}} = "Tab. Calmora 10 mg · 0+0+1 · ঘুমের জন্য"   (a line whose paper itself prints what it is for)
#   a stored lab "Creatinine" (1.8 mg/dL, 0.7–1.3) and the patient "Ma".
# flag: AnswerCheck reports a medicine_purpose code; pass: it reports none (other codes may still refuse a pass row: this
# corpus asserts only the purpose rule, as dose-change-corpus.tsv asserts only the dose rule).
# question rows decide the route (MedicinePurposeGuard.route): code = a code-built reply, zero model calls; mixed = the
# question also asks something else, so it goes to the model with the checks and code still appends chat.purpose.ask;
# none = not a purpose question. The stored medicine names are demoprol and calmora; the stored lab is creatinine.
# Fictional medicines only (Demoprol, Calmora); Napa and Metformin are named as a family would type them.
